examples.en: I got a new game console for my birthday.

examples.ko: 휴대용 게임기는 여행 갈 때 편해요.
examples.en: A handheld game console is convenient for trips.
The console suddenly turned off and I was startled.

examples.ko: 동생과 거실에서 게임기로 레이싱 게임을 했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling and I played a racing game on the console in the living room.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 게임기 가격이 다른 곳보다 싸요.
examples.en: This store has lower console prices than other places.

examples.ko: 게임기에 연결한 텔레비전 화면이 아주 선명해요.
examples.en: The TV screen connected to the console is very sharp.

explain: 텔레비전에 연결하는 큰 기계도, 손에 들고 하는 작은 기계도 게임기라고 불러요. 휴대폰으로 하는 게임은 게임기가 아니라 '모바일 게임'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I saved my allowance and bought a game console.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 살 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for buying the device.

phrases.en: I connected the game console to the TV.
phrases.nuance_ko: 텔레비전에 이어서 쓰는 큰 기계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the larger consoles that plug into a TV.

phrases.en: The game console broke, so I sent it for repair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 작동하지 않을 때 '고장 나다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '고장 나다' is used when a machine stops working.

explain_en: Both the big box that connects to a TV and the small device you hold are called 게임기. Games played on a phone are called 모바일 게임, not 게임기.

examples.en: That child stands out because of the blonde hair.
My younger sibling dyed their hair blonde.
A blonde-haired actor came onto the stage.
My hair was blonde as a child, but now it's brown.
The doll's blonde hair sparkles in the sunlight.
I was told blonde hair suits me well.

explain: '금발 머리'처럼 '머리'를 붙여 말하기도 해요. 한자로 '금'은 금색, '발'은 머리카락이에요. 염색이나 탈색으로 밝게 한 머리는 '금발로 염색하다', '탈색하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: A child with blonde hair is playing in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: '금발'과 뜻이 같아요. '머리'를 붙이면 머리카락 이야기라는 것이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as 금발. Adding 머리 makes it clearer that you are talking about hair.

phrases.en: Blonde hair really suits my older sister.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리 색이 사람과 잘 맞는다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to compliment how a hair color suits someone.

phrases.en: My friend dyed her hair blonde.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 금발이 아닌 머리를 염색해서 금발로 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when someone dyes non-blonde hair blonde.

explain_en: People also say '금발 머리' with '머리' added. In the Sino-Korean parts, '금' is gold and '발' is hair. Hair lightened by dyeing or bleaching is described with '금발로 염색하다' or '탈색하다'.

examples.en: The content of the call is recorded automatically.
I was surprised that my voice was recorded.

examples.ko: 수업이 녹음돼서 다시 들을 수 있어요.
examples.en: The class is recorded, so you can listen again.
I sent the recorded song to my friend.
I didn't know the meeting was being recorded.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 소리가 녹음될 때 빨간 불이 켜져요.
examples.en: This app shows a red light when sound is being recorded.

explain: '녹음하다'는 사람이 하는 일이고, '녹음되다'는 소리가 저절로 저장된 상태를 말해요. 전화, 수업, 회의처럼 기록이 남는 상황에 자주 나와요. 영상은 '녹화되다', 화면은 '캡처되다'로 구분해서 말해요.

phrases.en: The meeting is being recorded right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 소리가 저장되는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the sound is being saved at this moment.

phrases.en: The sound was too quiet, so it wasn't recorded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 저장되지 못했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the sound failed to be saved.

phrases.example: 이 마이크로는 작은 소리도 잘 녹음돼요.
phrases.en: Even small sounds are recorded well with this microphone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 깨끗하게 저장될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when sound is saved clearly.

explain_en: 녹음하다 is something a person does, while 녹음되다 describes sound that has been saved. It often appears with calls, classes and meetings. For video you say 녹화되다, and for a screen you say 캡처되다.

dis.h: be captured as sound or audio

p.n: 기록되다 means a written or logged record, not an audio recording.

examples.en: The department store is having a big year-end sale.
I bought winter clothes during the big sale.
They say everything is on big discount this weekend.
It was a big sale, so there were really a lot of people.
I heard the big sale only runs until Sunday.
I waited to buy a laptop to coincide with the big sale.

explain: '대-'가 붙어 할인 폭이나 규모가 크다는 느낌을 줘요. 가게 광고에서 많이 보이고 같은 상황에서 '세일'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: There is a big discount event this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 백화점의 큰 할인 이벤트를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a large sale event at a store or department store.

phrases.en: That store has a big sale at the end of the year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게가 할인을 한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a shop is running a big discount.

phrases.en: Shoes are on sale from today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대할인'보다 가볍고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter than 대할인 and used more in everyday talk.

explain_en: The prefix '대-' gives a feeling of a large discount or scale. It shows up a lot in store ads, and in the same situation people also say '세일'.

examples.en: A strange rumor is going around the company.
That rumor is not true.
I don't believe rumors easily.
Don't pay too much attention to rumors.
What started as a small rumor grew big.
Rumors also spread very fast.

explain: '소문'이 일상에서 가장 흔한 말이고, '루머'는 근거 없는 이야기라는 느낌이 더 강해요. '소문이 돌다', '루머가 돌다'처럼 '돌다'와 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Did you hear that rumor?
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가장 흔한 말이고, '루머'만큼 나쁜 느낌이 강하지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common everyday word, less negative than 'rumor'.

phrases.en: I don't believe that kind of rumor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들은 이야기를 사실로 받아들일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when accepting what you heard as true.

phrases.example: 근거 없는 루머에 신경 쓰지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't worry about groundless rumors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실이 아닌 이야기라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the meaning that the story isn't true.

explain_en: '소문' is the everyday word, while '루머' feels more like groundless talk. Both pair with '돌다': '소문이 돌다', '루머가 돌다'.

examples.en: This drama airs every Saturday.
That news was broadcast nationwide yesterday.

examples.ko: 새 예능 프로그램이 다음 달부터 방송될 거예요.
examples.en: The new variety show will start airing next month.
I drive while listening to music broadcast on the radio.
This scene was cut before it aired.
The final episode aired and everyone cried.

explain: '방송하다'는 만드는 쪽이 내보내는 것이고, '방송되다'는 프로그램이 나가는 것이에요. TV 드라마는 '방영되다'라고도 하는데, '방송되다'는 라디오 같은 소리 방송에도 써요. 말로는 '몇 시에 해요?'처럼 '하다'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: That drama will air next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: TV 프로그램에 주로 써요. 라디오에는 '방송되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mostly used for TV programs; for radio, use 방송되다.

phrases.en: That program is being broadcast now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 나가고 있는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is on the air right now.

phrases.en: Do you know when the drama is on?
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 방송이 나가는 때를 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -는 to ask about the time a show airs.

explain_en: '방송하다' is the side that sends it out; '방송되다' is the program going out. TV dramas can also be '방영되다', but '방송되다' works for audio broadcasts like radio too. In speech, people often just say '몇 시에 해요?' with '하다'.

dis.h: aired on TV or radio, any content

p.n: 방영되다 is for shows or films on screen, so it does not fit radio news.

en: to be unnatural; to be affected

examples.en: That actor's acting is a bit unnatural.
His expression was unnatural, so he seemed to be lying.
Please fix the parts where the translation is unnatural.
It felt unnatural because the mood changed suddenly.
They were new shoes, so I walked awkwardly.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 한국어 발음은 부자연스럽지 않아요.
examples.en: That person's Korean pronunciation isn't unnatural.

explain: '자연스럽다'의 반대말이에요. 말, 표정, 동작이 꾸민 듯하거나 이상할 때 써요. '어색하다'와 비슷하지만 '어색하다'는 사람 사이의 분위기에도 많이 쓰고, ㅂ 불규칙이라 '부자연스러워요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: He gave an unnatural smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 꾸밀 때는 '부자연스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it changes to 부자연스러운.

phrases.en: That translation does not sound unnatural.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어색하지 않고 괜찮다고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says something is not awkward and is fine.

phrases.en: The mood is awkward because we just met.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 사이의 분위기에는 '부자연스럽다'보다 '어색하다'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For the mood between people, 어색하다 is used more than 부자연스럽다.

explain_en: It is the opposite of '자연스럽다'. You use it when speech, expressions or movements seem forced or odd. It is close to '어색하다', which is also widely used for the mood between people. As a ㅂ-irregular adjective, it becomes '부자연스러워요'.

examples.en: Every morning I hear birdsong outside the window.
Today I woke up to birdsong.
I listened to birdsong while walking along the forest path.
Just listening to birdsong makes my mind feel calm.

examples.ko: 새소리 알람으로 바꿨더니 기분 좋게 일어나요.
examples.en: Since I changed to a birdsong alarm, I wake up in a good mood.

examples.ko: 산에 오르니 새소리 말고는 아무 소리도 안 났어요.
examples.en: When I climbed the mountain, there was no sound except birdsong.

explain: '새소리가 들리다', '새가 지저귀다'처럼 함께 쓰면 자연스러워요. '새 울음소리'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '새소리'가 더 짧고 흔해요. '새'와 '소리'를 붙여서 한 단어로 써요.

phrases.en: As soon as I entered the forest, I heard birdsong from all around.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새소리가 들리다'는 듣는 사람 쪽에서, '새소리가 나다'는 소리가 생기는 쪽에서 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '새소리가 들리다' is from the listener's side, while '새소리가 나다' focuses on the sound occurring.
phrases.en_equiv: birdsong is heard / there is birdsong

phrases.en: Listening to birdsong in the park makes me feel good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 귀를 기울여 듣는 느낌으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you listen to the birdsong on purpose or with enjoyment.

phrases.example: 밤에 새 울음소리가 크게 들려서 깼어요.
phrases.en: I woke up because I heard a bird's cry loudly at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새소리'와 뜻은 같지만 조금 더 길고, 새가 우는 소리를 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '새소리' but longer, and it emphasizes the bird's crying sound.

explain_en: It sounds natural in '새소리가 들리다' and '새가 지저귀다' (birds chirp). '새 울음소리' also exists, but '새소리' is shorter and more common in daily life. '새' and '소리' are written together as one word.

en: to have a doubt; to doubt; to be doubtful of

examples.en: I doubt whether that's really true.
The result was strange, so it raised suspicion.
If you suspect a cold, go to the hospital.
If there's anything doubtful, please tell me.
This file is suspected to have a virus.
When in doubt, check again.

explain: '의심되다'는 '~이/가 의심되다'처럼 나쁜 일이나 거짓일 수 있다는 생각이 저절로 들 때 써요. 내가 일부러 의심하면 '의심하다'예요. 병원에서는 '감기가 의심되다'처럼 아직 확실하지 않은 병에 말해요.

phrases.en: I have a doubt whether that story is a lie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의심하는 마음이 저절로 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when doubt arises on its own.

phrases.en: If there is anything doubtful, please tell me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이상하게 느껴지는 부분을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Points to the parts that seem odd.

phrases.en: I don't doubt that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 일부러 의심할 때는 '의심하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '의심하다' when you doubt on purpose.

explain_en: 의심되다 is used as '~이/가 의심되다' when a thought that something may be bad or false comes to mind by itself. If you doubt on purpose, it is 의심하다. At a clinic it is used for a not-yet-certain illness, as in '감기가 의심되다'.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 전원을 켜면 바로 작동돼요.
examples.en: This machine runs as soon as you turn the power on.
The elevator hasn't worked since yesterday.
I'll check whether the app worked properly.
When the emergency bell goes off, it makes a loud sound.
Not a single computer works.

examples.ko: 이 시계는 배터리 없이도 작동될 거예요.
examples.en: This watch will run even without a battery.

explain: 기계나 프로그램이 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '작동하다'도 써요. 안 될 때는 '작동이 안 돼요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: This watch works well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작동되다'와 같은 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with the same meaning as '작동되다'.

phrases.en: The computer suddenly won't work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 안 움직일 때 가장 흔히 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say a machine isn't working.

phrases.en: The machine operates normally.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제없이 움직인다는 뜻으로 설명서에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it runs without trouble; common in manuals.

explain_en: Use it for machines or programs that are running. '작동하다' works the same way. When something fails, you say '작동이 안 돼요'.

examples.en: During my trip I saw dairy cows at a ranch.
A dairy cow produces a lot of milk a day.
Every morning I give hay to the dairy cows.
The dairy cow is eating grass in the field.
I tried making cheese at a dairy farm.

examples.ko: 검은색과 흰색 무늬가 있는 젖소가 귀여워요.
examples.en: The black and white dairy cow is cute.

explain: '한우'는 주로 고기를 위해 키우는 한국 소이고, 젖소는 우유를 위해 키우는 소예요. 한국 사람들은 얼룩무늬 소를 보면 보통 젖소를 떠올려요. 발음은 [젇쏘]예요.

phrases.en: There are about ten dairy cows on the farm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소는 '마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Cows are counted with 'mari'.

phrases.en: I went to a dairy farm with my family on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젖소를 키우는 곳을 말할 때 '목장'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'farm' to talk about a place that raises dairy cows.

phrases.en: My uncle raises dairy cows in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우유를 얻으려고 소를 기를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for raising cows to get milk.

explain_en: 'Hanu' is the Korean beef cattle raised mainly for meat, while 'jeotso' is raised for milk. Koreans usually picture a spotted cow when they hear jeotso. It is pronounced [jeot-sso].

en: to be investigated; to be surveyed

examples.en: The cause of the accident is still being investigated.
This case has been under investigation since yesterday.

examples.ko: 조사된 결과를 보면 학생이 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: According to the survey results, the number of students dropped a lot.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 다음 달에 자세히 조사될 거예요.
examples.en: This issue will be looked into in detail next month.
Once people's opinions are surveyed, we'll decide then.

examples.ko: 이 병은 아직 원인이 조사되지 않았어요.
examples.en: The cause of this disease hasn't been investigated yet.

explain: '조사하다'는 사람이 살펴보는 것이고, '조사되다'는 조사의 대상이 되어 결과가 나오는 것이에요. 사고·사건 조사와 설문 조사에 모두 써요. 한국어 문법의 '조사'(을/를, 이/가)와 소리가 같아서 앞뒤 말을 보고 구분해요.

phrases.en: The investigated results are posted on the internet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 '조사해서 나온 것'을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies a noun to mean what came out of the investigation.

phrases.example: 학생의 절반이 아침을 안 먹는 것으로 조사됐어요.
phrases.en: The survey found that half of the students skip breakfast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 설문 결과를 전할 때 자주 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pattern often used to report news or survey results.
phrases.en_equiv: was found by survey to be

phrases.en: The cause hasn't been investigated yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 조사가 끝나지 않았다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying the investigation isn't done yet.

explain_en: '조사하다' is a person looking into something; '조사되다' is being the subject of an investigation or survey and having results come out. It covers both accident or case investigations and opinion surveys. The same sound is also the grammar term '조사' (particles like 을/를, 이/가), so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: The doctor diagnosed my symptoms.
The mechanic is diagnosing the cause of the breakdown.

examples.ko: 의사가 단순한 감기로 진단한 환자가 많아요.
examples.en: Many patients were diagnosed by the doctor as having just a cold.
You first have to diagnose the problem exactly.
There is a program that diagnoses the state of a computer.

examples.ko: 선생님이 제 한국어 실력을 진단해 줬어요.
examples.en: My teacher assessed my Korean level for me.

explain: '진단을 받다'는 환자가, '진단하다'는 의사가 주어예요. 병뿐 아니라 기계, 회사, 실력처럼 문제를 살펴볼 때도 비유로 써요. '검사하다'는 살펴보는 일이고, '진단하다'는 결과를 보고 판단까지 내려요.

phrases.en: I was diagnosed with a cold at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자가 주어일 때 써요. 의사가 주어이면 '진단하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the patient is the subject. When the doctor is the subject, use '진단하다'.

phrases.example: 의사 선생님이 제 몸 상태를 진단해 줬어요.
phrases.en: The doctor diagnosed my condition for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주다'를 붙이면 나를 위해 해 준다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-a/eo juda' gives the feeling that it was done for me.

phrases.en: An expert diagnosed the company's problems.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 아니라 문제의 원인을 살펴보고 판단할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is also used for examining and judging the cause of a problem, not just illness.

explain_en: The patient says '진단을 받다' and the doctor '진단하다'. Beyond illness, it is also used figuratively for examining machines, companies, or skills. '검사하다' is the checking itself, while '진단하다' goes on to make a judgment from the result.

examples.ko: 친부모를 찾고 싶어서 입양 기관에 문의했어요.
examples.en: I wanted to find my biological parents, so I contacted an adoption agency.
My adoptive parents loved me as much as my biological parents would have.
It has been a long time since I lost contact with my biological parents.
You have to write your biological parents' names on the form.
I still don't know who my biological parents are.
My younger sibling grew up beside the biological parents.

explain: 입양이나 재혼 이야기에서 낳아 준 부모를 말할 때 써요. 짝말은 '양부모'(입양한 부모)이고, 높여서 말하면 '친부모님'이에요. 일반 대화에서 그냥 '부모님'이라고 하면 이런 구분이 없어요.

phrases.en: My biological parents live abroad now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '친부모'를 높여서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The respectful form of 'biological parents'.

phrases.en: He met his biological parents when he grew up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입양된 사람이 낳아 준 부모를 처음 만나는 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in stories where an adopted person meets their birth parents.

phrases.en: I want to know my birth parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: '친부모'를 쉬운 말로 풀어서 한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language way to say 'biological parents'.
phrases.en_equiv: the parents who gave birth to me

explain_en: It is used in talk about adoption or remarriage to mean the parents who gave birth to you. The opposite is '양부모' (adoptive parents), and the polite form is '친부모님'. In normal conversation, plain '부모님' carries no such distinction.

en: to absorb; to soak; to consume

examples.en: A sponge absorbs water.
The plant took in water through its roots.

examples.ko: 우리 몸은 비타민을 장에서 흡수하고 나머지는 내보내요.
examples.en: Our body absorbs vitamins in the intestines and sends out the rest.

examples.ko: 아이들은 새로운 지식을 빠르게 흡수하는 편이에요.
examples.en: Children tend to absorb new knowledge quickly.
This fabric can't absorb sweat.

examples.ko: 큰 회사가 작은 회사를 흡수할 거예요.
examples.en: The big company will absorb the small one.

explain: 물이나 영양분이 스며드는 것뿐 아니라 지식, 문화를 받아들이는 것에도 써요. 회사가 다른 회사를 합칠 때도 '흡수하다'를 써요. 물건이 물을 빨아들이는 것은 일상에서 '빨아들이다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: This towel soaks up water well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 물을 빨아들이는 것은 일상에서 '흡수하다'보다 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For things soaking up water, this is more common than 흡수하다 in daily speech.

phrases.en: The medicine is absorbed into the body quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받아들여지는 쪽이 주어일 때는 '흡수하다' 대신 '흡수되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: When the thing being absorbed is the subject, use 흡수되다 instead of 흡수하다.

phrases.en: Children absorb a new culture quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 아니라 지식이나 문화를 받아들일 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for taking in knowledge or culture rather than water.

explain_en: Besides water and nutrients soaking in, it is used for taking in knowledge or culture, and for a company merging another one into itself. In everyday talk a thing drawing in water can also be called 빨아들이다.
